source.title: HDBSCAN is Surprisingly Effective at Finding Interpretable Clusters of the SAE Decoder Matrix

record.tranche_reason: The post discusses feature splitting and proposes interpreting decoder-matrix clusters as reverse splitting, but it does not compare SAE dictionary sizes or test whether clusters map to parent features, partition their inputs, or form a nested hierarchy.
record.gate_note: The reported clustering results concern semantic coherence of clusters within individual SAE decoder matrices. They do not test the size-dependent splitting behavior or the parent-child relationships named in the claim versions. The reported noise percentages and cross-layer UMAP similarities likewise do not test those versions.
record.test_reason: The post clusters decoder vectors within single fixed-size (16K) SAEs on GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2-2B. It never compares dictionary sizes, parent and child latents, firing behaviour or training objectives. 'Reverse feature splitting' and absorption appear only as a conceptual proposal and open question, so its results do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that the cardinal-direction cluster 888 is an instance of Bricken et al.'s 'Bug 2', where multiple latents stand for one feature. They suggest clusters could act as proxies for smaller-SAE features without training SAEs of varying sizes, but they leave this untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study clusters decoder-matrix vectors within individual SAEs using HDBSCAN and cosine similarity; it does not train or compare SAEs of different dictionary sizes. The post says it is work in progress and hopes to release the clusters and code.
record.method_sensitivity: The fraction classified as noise varies by layer and clustering hyperparameters: the post reports the best GPT2-Small result at layer 4 and says even the last layer can have high noise depending on hyperparameters. It also reports qualitatively similar UMAPs in some layer blocks.

fits_no_version.finding: HDBSCAN on cosine distances between 16K-SAE decoder vectors yields some semantically coherent clusters (directions, 'side', days of the week, cooking). However, over 90% of features are labelled noise in Gemma-2-2B, and at best about 35% are clustered in GPT-2 Small (layer 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clustering decoder vectors within a single SAE recovers a small fraction of features as interpretable families.

record.problems: The post describes the work as in progress. It reports that more than 90% of features are classified as noise across Gemma-2-2B layers and that at best about 35% are clustered for GPT2-Small, at one layer. The showcased cluster interpretations are qualitative, and the post does not validate the proposed reverse-splitting relationship with comparisons across SAE sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the reported noise proportions or qualitative UMAP layer-block similarities: these do not measure the size-dependent splitting or parent-child feature relationships in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No SAEs of different dictionary sizes are compared. Coverage of a coarse feature's inputs and directional proximity to it are not measured.
No splitting test across sizes in GPT-2 Small, Gemma-2 or open releases. The jbloom and GemmaScope 16K SAEs are only clustered.
The authors ask whether a general-to-specific hierarchy exists but report no nested families or hierarchy test. HDBSCAN clusters are flat groups.
Absorption is described conceptually only. No parent or child firing is measured.
Larger-SAE latents are not compared against smaller-SAE latents, and novel latents are not examined.
No comparison of training objectives, and no Matryoshka SAEs.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal work-in-progress LessWrong post. The interpretations are qualitative and based on GPT-4o-mini autointerp, with no baselines or controls. The noise fractions and the cross-layer UMAP similarities concern clustering quality, not splitting, so leaving them out of the rows is justified. The prose lists feature 489 for cluster 496 while the table lists 498; this is unresolved in the post.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE dictionary-size comparison or measurement of smaller-to-larger feature replacements, input coverage, or directional proximity.
No size-dependent splitting test across large models or open SAE releases.
The post clusters features within individual SAEs but does not test nested families, parent-child geometry, or whether families mirror a hierarchy of concepts.
Absorption and parent-child firing differences are described conceptually; no firing behavior is measured.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents, combinations of latents, or novel latents.
No test of whether SAE objectives produce splitting, and no comparison with Matryoshka or other objectives.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied HDBSCAN to decoder-matrix feature vectors using cosine similarity and interpreted a resulting cluster.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of the clustered features, as described by the authors.
rows.value: The 17-feature cluster is described as cardinal directions, including north, south, east, west, and northeast.
rows.note: The post gives examples of individual features activating on directional terms and interprets the cluster as a family.
rows.check: This is a within-SAE cluster description, and 'observed' refers only to semantic coherence, not to any claim version. The authors link it to Bricken et al.'s Bug 2 (multiple latents for one feature), but they test no smaller SAE to confirm it.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied HDBSCAN to decoder-matrix feature vectors using cosine similarity and interpreted a resulting cluster.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of the clustered features, as described by the authors.
rows.value: The five-feature cluster is described as covering different uses and variations of “side.”
rows.note: The feature list in the prose includes 489, while the accompanying table lists 498; the post does not resolve this discrepancy.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied HDBSCAN to decoder-matrix feature vectors using cosine similarity and interpreted a resulting cluster.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of the clustered features, as described by the authors.
rows.value: The eight-feature cluster is described as relating to different days of the week, plus one feature for “Yesterday.”
rows.note: The authors also report that a 2D PCA of these features showed the non-linearity discussed in the cited work.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied HDBSCAN to decoder-matrix feature vectors using cosine similarity and interpreted a resulting cluster.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of the clustered features, as described by the authors.
rows.value: The 11-feature cluster is interpreted as primarily related to culinary processes and ingredients, despite some individually unclear or apparently unrelated feature explanations.
rows.note: The authors say the cluster meaning becomes apparent when the features are considered together.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied HDBSCAN to decoder-matrix feature vectors and identified an additional cluster.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of the clustered features, as described by the authors.
rows.value: The cluster is described as activating on different kinds of “points,” including percentages, scores, and directions.
rows.note: The post names this as another similar cluster but gives no feature list or further measurements.
rows.check: This is a passing mention with no feature list or measure, so the 'observed' state has nothing behind it. It is a qualitative within-SAE cluster, not a splitting result. The locator should say it appears inside the Cluster 496 discussion.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
